# AM9517_4PC - Am9517A-4 multimode DMA controller, four channels, 4 MHz grade, molded (plastic) DIP

Package DIP-40 · family MOS LSI · catalogue file [catalog/chips/AM9517_4PC.json](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/RetroSchematic/blob/master/src/catalog/chips/AM9517_4PC.json)

| 1 | /IOR | output |  | three-state | I/O read, bidirectional active low three-state: in the Idle cycle an input used by the CPU to read the control registers; in the Active cycle an output used to read data from a peripheral during a DMA Write transfer |
| 2 | /IOW | output |  | three-state | I/O write, bidirectional active low three-state: in the Idle cycle an input used by the CPU to load the controller; in the Active cycle an output used to load data into a peripheral during a DMA Read transfer. A CPU write needs a rising IOW edge after each byte; holding IOW low and toggling CS is not enough |

## Functions

| Output pin | What it does |
|---|---|
| 21-23,26-30 | DB0-DB7: in the Program Condition (Idle cycle, CS low, HACK low) the CPU reads or writes the register picked by A3-A0 with IOR or IOW (figures 4 and 5). In DMA cycles: address A8-A15 in state S1 for the external latch; Temporary register data in memory-to-memory transfers. |
| 1-4,32-35,37-40 | Active cycle: A0-A7 give the low address byte; MEMR/IOW (Read transfer, memory to I/O), IOR/MEMW (Write transfer, I/O to memory), or neither (Verify transfer). Memory-to-memory: channel 0 is the source, channel 1 the destination, eight states per byte (S11-S14 read, S21-S24 write). Normally each transfer takes states S2, S3, S4 (S3 dropped with compressed timing); S1 is used only when A8-A15 must change. |
| 8,9,10,14,15,24,25,36 | Handshake: an unmasked DREQ (or software request) raises HREQ; on HACK the controller enters the Active cycle (S0, S1...), raises AEN, strobes ADSTB, and asserts the DACK of the highest-priority requesting channel. EOP is pulsed low at TC. |

## Stored state

Changes on: CLK; CPU register writes and reads in the Program Condition; DREQ, HACK, EOP; RESET

- Idle cycle (S1): DREQ lines sampled every clock; CS sampled; CS low with HACK low enters the Program Condition.
- Active cycle states: S0 waits for HACK after HREQ; S1 updates A8-A15; S2, S3, S4 are the working states; SW wait states are inserted before S4 by READY.
- Command register (cleared by reset): bit 0 memory-to-memory enable; bit 1 channel 0 address hold enable (X if bit 0 = 0); bit 2 controller disable; bit 3 compressed timing (X if bit 0 = 1); bit 4 rotating priority (0 = fixed); bit 5 extended write selection (0 = late write; X if bit 3 = 1); bit 6 DREQ sense active low (0 = active high); bit 7 DACK sense active high (0 = active low).
- Mode register (per channel): bits 1-0 channel select; bits 3-2 00 verify, 01 write, 10 read transfer, 11 illegal (XX if bits 7-6 = 11); bit 4 autoinitialize enable; bit 5 address decrement (0 = increment); bits 7-6 00 demand, 01 single, 10 block, 11 cascade mode.
- Request register: bits 1-0 channel, bit 2 set (1) or reset (0) the request bit. Software requests are serviced only in Block mode; all are cleared by reset.
- Mask register: single bit command bits 1-0 channel, bit 2 set/clear; all-bits command bits 0-3 for channels 0-3; set by reset and by EOP of a channel not in autoinitialize.
- Status register: bits 0-3 channel 0-3 has reached TC (cleared by reset and by each status read); bits 4-7 channel 0-3 request pending.
- Register addressing (CS low): A3 = 1 selects the control registers: 1000 IOR read status, IOW write command; 1001 IOW write request; 1010 IOW write single mask bit; 1011 IOW write mode; 1100 IOW clear byte pointer flip-flop; 1101 IOR read temporary, IOW master clear; 1111 IOW write all mask bits; other combinations illegal. A3 = 0: A2 A1 channel, A0 = 0 address, A0 = 1 word count; write goes to base and current, read gives current; first/last flip-flop 0 = low byte, 1 = high byte.
- Master clear (software) = hardware reset. Clear first/last flip-flop: next access is the low byte.
- Single transfer mode: one byte per HREQ/HACK handshake; DREQ must be held until DACK; if DREQ stays active HREQ goes inactive and a new transfer follows on the next rising HACK edge.
- Block transfer mode: transfers until TC or external EOP; DREQ need only be held until DACK goes active.
- Demand transfer mode: transfers until TC, external EOP, or DREQ goes inactive.
- Cascade mode: HREQ/HACK of another Am9517A are connected to DREQ/DACK of this channel; the channel then outputs no address or control signals of its own.
- Current word count returns one less than the number of words; at zero a TC is generated; after an internally generated EOP the count reads FFFF.
- Autoinitialize: after EOP the current address and current word count are restored from the base registers and the mask bit is not set.
- Fixed priority: channel 0 highest, 3 lowest. Rotating: the channel last served becomes the lowest. The priority encoder picks the channel on each active-going HACK edge; a running channel is not suspended by a higher-priority request.
- Address generation: A8-A15 are output on the data lines only in S1, and S1 occurs only when a carry or borrow from A7 to A8 happens (block and demand modes).
- Memory-to-memory: started by a software request for channel 0; EOP is output at TC of channel 1; channel 0 may hold a fixed address (Command bit 1) to fill a block with one word.

## Electrical

| Value | Figure |
|---|---|
| outputLowMaxCurrentMa | 3.2 |
| outputHighMaxCurrentMa | -0.2 |
| inputSchmitt | no |
| notes | Electrical characteristics (page 9), VCC 5 V +-5%, 0..70 C: VOH 2.4 V min at -200 uA (3.3 V at -100 uA, HREQ only); VOL 0.4 V max at IOL 3.2 mA; VIH 2.0 V min, VIL 0.8 V max; input load and output leakage -10..+10 uA; ICC 75 mA typ, 150 mA max at 0 C. Capacitance output 4/8 pF, input 8/15 pF, I/O 10/18 pF (typ/max). EOP is open drain: 3.3K or 4.7K pull-up, cannot sink a 1K pull-up's current. Absolute maximum: -0.5..+7 V on VCC and signals, 1.5 W. Output loading for timing: one standard TTL gate plus 50 pF (data bus 15 pF min, 100 pF max). |

## Not known

- Whether DACK0-DACK3, HREQ, AEN and ADSTB are push-pull: the signal description calls them 'Output' without saying three-state or open drain; stored as totem-pole.
- Contents of the address, word count and mode registers after reset or power-on: not stated (reset clears only command, status, request, temporary and the first/last flip-flop and sets the mask).

## Notes

Card 3207 position 26F, marked AM9517_4PC = Am9517A-4 in the plastic package (ordering information p1: Am9517A-4DC/PC, 4 MHz). Only the Am9517A-4 column of the switching tables is used. Pin 5 is named PIN5 because the sheet gives it no name, only note 11.
